text:
alice: seeing big p99 spike for inference in eu-west-1 (gpu-pool-*.svc). started ~09:12 UTC, entire pool affected
ben: yup dashboards show host->host packet loss increase and retransmits around the same time
alice: traces point to net tx queuing, KV cache timeouts causing higher compute wait
carla: can you paste `ip link` + `tc qdisc show` from one of the hosts?
alice: paste below from host gpu-node-17:
```
$ ip link show dev eth0
4: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1400 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 7a:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ tc qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc tbf 1: root tbf rate 900mbit burst 1540b limit 1400b
```
ben: mtu 1400 on hosts that should be 9000 (we use jumbo frames + RDMA), that'll force fragmentation and likely break mlx5/RDMA paths
carla: check dmesg on same host, saw mlx5 warnings:
```
[  123.456789] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: frag_list rx failed, dropping
[  123.456790] rdma_ucm: fallback to kernel tcp path
```
ben: that fallback explains the sharp latency jump — RDMA path optimized for intra-node/east-west traffic is being bypassed
infra-bot: deploy event: `net-policies/egress-shaping` applied to node-pool-eu-west by autoscaler at 08:58 UTC (change-id: ch_2026_3412)
alice: oh — autoscaler applied egress shaping as a temporary protect during noisy-tenant incident. but the selector hit gpu pool due to missing label in policy
dan: that was my change, i scoped it too wide. i intended to target `tenant=best-effort` but used `role=worker` by mistake. rolling out revert now
sre_oncall: tagging this P1 since inference SLOs are impacted, can we do an immediate hotfix?
carla: hotfix plan:
- remove the TBF qdisc from active nodes: `sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root`
- restore mtu to 9000: `sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000`
- restart mlx5 modules if needed: `sudo systemctl restart rdma` (careful, drains network briefly)
- run quick perf check: `iperf3 -c <peer> -P 4 -t 10` and `rdma_bw` to confirm RDMA path
alice: i'm doing canary on gpu-node-17 now — removing qdisc and setting mtu back
ben: heads up for kube pods: we'll drain and cordon node during fix to avoid in-progress inference requests failing — use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets`
dan: reverted netpolicy in git and applied. policy now targets `tenant=best-effort` only.
infra-bot: revert applied (ch_2026_3412-revert) at 09:26 UTC
alice: removed tbf, set mtu=9000, restarted rdma. dmesg now: `mlx5_core: RDMA device initialized`, rdma path restored
carla: iperf3 shows baseline bandwidth restored, no fragmentation. p99 on canary node dropped back to normal within ~45s
sre_oncall: good. plan for full rollout: schedule rolling uncordon/fix across gpu pool with 5-host concurrency, monitor for 1h, then promote to 20-host batches if stable
dan: agreed. will push cron job to validate selectors to avoid this class of error
ben: also add an alert that fires when host MTU != 9000 for gpu-pool hosts and when tc qdisc contains tbf on eth0 for >30s
alice: adding wiki note with commands and postmortem after wrap-up. thanks for quick responses :thumbsup:
carla: root cause summary: autoscaler netpolicy applied a host-level egress shaping TBF with MTU/limit mismatch that caused fragmentation and RDMA fallback -> increased east-west latency and packet loss -> inference p99 SLO regressions.
ben: mitigation: revert policy, remove qdisc, restore mtu, restart RDMA, canary then rolling update.
infra-bot: incident closed (provisional) at 09:52 UTC — monitoring for recurrence
`reacted with :eyes: by dan`
